## Problem

## Word Search II

Coding interview, onsite software-engineering round, reported in April 2026.

You are given a two-dimensional character array `board` along with an array of strings named `words`. Return every string from `words` that can be found in the board.

A string is considered found when its letters can be traced through cells that share a horizontal or vertical edge. While building one word, no board position can be visited twice.

### Examples

Example 1:

```text
Input:
`board = [
["m","o","o","n"],
["s","t","a","r"],
["p","l","a","n"],
["c","l","o","u"]
],
words = ["moon","star","plan","clou","stone"]`

Output: ["moon","star","plan","clou"]
```

Explanation: Each returned word can be followed through edge-adjacent cells, whereas `stone` cannot be traced on this board.

Example 2:

```text
Input:
`board = [
["p","q"],
["p","q"]
],
words = ["pqpqp"]`

Output: []
```

Explanation: Forming this five-letter word would require revisiting a cell because the board contains only four cells.

### Constraints

* `1 <= board.length, board[i].length <= 12`
* Every `board[i]` contains lowercase English letters only.
* `1 <= words.length <= 30,000`
* `1 <= words[i].length <= 10`
* Each `words[i]` is made up exclusively of lowercase English letters.
* No two entries in `words` are the same.

### Company Notes

This problem was reported as LeetCode 212 during a software-engineer phone interview.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

This is a multi-pattern search problem, think of using a trie to store all words and then backtracking on the board.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use DFS from each cell, pruning when the current prefix is not in the trie.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The complexity is O(M*N*4^L) in the worst case, but the trie prunes many branches, watch for duplicate words in the result.

</details>
